question_record.context: A sequence of alerts indicating potential human-operated malicious activity were observed on the device `vnevado-win10v`. Initially, a known credential theft tool `mimikatz.exe` was executed, followed by the possible use of the Rubeus kerberoasting tool. Lastly, a remote session dropped and launched a file, which might suggest an attacker or malware attempting lateral movement or propagation.
question_record.question: What was the process and its details that were dropped and launched from a remote session as observed in the final alert?
solution: A known credential theft tool was executed by the account named `tgs2z`.
The tool `rubeus.exe`, which can perform kerberoasting and pass-the-ticket attacks, was detected.
There was potential human-operated malicious activity originating from IP address `141.216.110.153`.
A remote session dropped and executed the process `psexesvc.exe` with Process ID `7668` at `2024-06-27t14:34:10.0201983z`.

89.name: Malicious credential theft tool execution detected
89.description:
A known credential theft tool execution command line was detected.
Either the process itself or its command line indicated an intent to dump users' credentials, keys, plain-text passwords and more.

107.name: Possible use of the Rubeus kerberoasting tool
107.description:
Activity indicating the use of the Rubeus tool was observed on this endpoint. This tool can perform kerberoasting, pass-the-ticket, and other attack techniques that take advantage of Kerberos authentication.

During these attacks, attackers often request Kerberos tickets for an account's service principal name (SPN). They then decrypt the tickets to get plaintext credentials associated with the account. Alternatively, they can perform the pass-the-ticket technique to authenticate directly without having to decrypt the obtained tickets.

105.name: Potential human-operated malicious activity
105.description: A sequence of alerts that might be indicative of human operated malicious activity was observed on this device. This activity might lead to ransomware or other payloads installed on target devices.

60.name: File dropped and launched from remote location
60.description: A remote session dropped a file and executed it. An attacker or a malware might be an attempting move laterally or propagate.
